tier_reason: Orchestrator correction (tier unchanged): point benchmark_url at the newer 2026-06-12 C++ report the verifier found; compiler and CPU still unstated.
Stays B (Glaze author's json_performance harness). Usability set to reference: HPND-sell-variant is not flagged OSI-approved by SPDX (BSD-3-Clause-Clear and BSD-3-Clause-Attribution precedents).

Downgraded C to D: enricher found the JSON writer never escapes strings and the YAML writer emits all strings unquoted, so the measured serialization gaps (3.3x vs nlohmann/RapidJSON, 98x/15x vs yaml-cpp) skip work the baselines do and the output is wrong for strings that need escaping (uniwidth and fast_resize precedents; kept as directional since the chart values are real measurements of a flawed writer).

corrections.caveats: Chart values only (serialization.cpp does real work) with compiler flags and CPU missing; typed-struct reflection vs generic DOM. The JSON writer never escapes strings and the native lexer leaves \n, \" and \uXXXX undecoded, so the 3.3x serialization gap skips the escape scan nlohmann and RapidJSON perform; the YAML writer emits every string unquoted, so the yaml-cpp rows are unequal work. Unknown keys throw std::runtime_error, doubles are written fixed with 9 decimals (lossy), round-trip tests use symbol-free strings only. The README claim that nlohmann and RapidJSON convert values lazily is wrong. Single 2.9 KB doc; proof of concept that points users to glaze. Archived 2026-08-20, last code change 2025-02-04.

tier_reason: Downgraded C to D: the nativejson-benchmark adapter discards atof()'s result, so the compiler very likely removed number conversion from the timed json.h parse (nlohmann converted numbers), and the stringify adapter formats pointer bits; the 2016 build also failed 16 conformance tests fixed later. Kept as directional (MQF-style no-op suspected but not confirmed by disassembly).

corrections.caveats: nativejson-benchmark 2016 run (clang 7.0, i7-4980HQ): the adapter sheredomjsonhtest.cpp calls atof() in ParseNumbers and discards the result, which LLVM 3.7 marks nounwind+readonly and deletes, so the canada.json parse very likely did no number conversion while nlohmann did (not confirmed by disassembly); WriteNumbers memcpy's the char* of json_number_s into a double, so stringify rows formatted pointer bits rather than document numbers. The measured build failed 9 of 34 validation tests and 7 of 9 string tests (conformance.csv), fixed later (\u decoding added, raw control characters rejected 2026-10-02). nlohmann v2.0.3 baseline from 2016. More than 15 closed issues report heap OOB, OOB reads and stack overflows (2022 to 2026-10-01, #132).

tier_reason: Stays C (first-party PARSING.md). Enricher caveat correction: the fast path is a sajson build whose number fidelity the bench input never exercises.

corrections.caveats: First-party PARSING.md numbers; since commit 3d45bc0 (2019-06-01) the finalized parser is sajson, so the 27682 ns figure is sajson plus lowering (the RapidJSON-backed figure was 66174 ns) and the 9.2x over an unversioned nlohmann is mostly sajson's win. use_sajson is OFF by default; the benchmark CMake enables it when sajson.h is found. sajson keeps only int32 integers (larger become doubles, precision lost above 2^53) and its doubles are not correctly rounded (28/66 double tests failed in 2016); the bench input (10 packets of about 1 KB, 150 small ints, no doubles) exercises neither. Dart rows use unsafe_ptr; the key-lookup counter is mis-scaled (ns column fine); the YAJL generator writes false for true; the finalized parse allocates json.size()*8. Compiler and CPU model unstated. Archived 2024-07-16; Apache-2.0.

tier_reason: Stays C. Enricher caveat correction: the measured build is unpublished (JSON_LIBRARY hides the benchmarked API) and the 12x lazy line times no parse.

corrections.caveats: mloskot/json_benchmark README (VC++ 11.0 32-bit only): 1.09x vs JsonCpp while RapidJSON is 5.5x faster on the same page. The libjson rows are not reproducible from public code: the shipped JSONOptions.h defines JSON_LIBRARY, which hides libjson::parse, so the measured build had unpublished edits (likely JSON_PREPARSE; 240 ms per canada.json fits an eager build); benchmark_libjson.cpp has one commit whose get_json() loaded only canada.json and HEAD calls a missing jb::get_json(). The lazy 0.478 s line is not a parse: the harness checks only the root type, set from the first character, so it timed a whitespace-strip copy plus node allocation and the 12x lazy claim is invalid. The 2013 rows predate the set_mark fix dff5b86 (2013-06-04). Default build keeps only the low byte of \uXXXX escapes, stores numbers as double via std::atof (bug #67); open crash tickets #55/#61, -std=c++11 break #63. BSD-2-Clause per libjson_7.6.1.zip; last release 2012-06-25, abandoned.

tier_reason: Stays A (nativejson-benchmark public harness). Enricher caveat correction: the 2016 margin is a canada.json effect and Boost.JSON's 2019 table shows tao-json 4.2-5.5x slower than nlohmann.

corrections.caveats: No performance claim from the project itself; the only A-grade numbers are the 2016 nativejson-benchmark run (taocpp/json submodule d380c63, before 1.0.0-beta.7; clang 7.0, i7-4980HQ) where the 1.8x parse over nlohmann v2.0.3 is mostly canada.json (citm_catalog 0.96x; without canada, parse 1.08x and stringify 1.21x) and tao-json is 5.2x slower than RapidJSON. Boost.JSON's doc/qbk/benchmarks.qbk (e73d488, 2019-10-23) lists tao-json and nlohmann in one table on the same inputs at 2056-2178 vs 491-495 ms and 22952-23265 vs 4195-4320 ms, so tao-json is about 4.2-5.5x slower than nlohmann there, with no harness, hardware or compiler published. The nativejson harness uses the removed tao::json::sax API, so the result cannot be re-run on current code. No nesting-depth limit (issue #121 stack overflow), DOM parse throws on duplicate keys, sorted std::map objects, peak memory 1.6-1.9x nlohmann, still pre-1.0 (beta.11).
